intersect.text: from the Enns (14.4 E) to the eastern edge of the Wienerwald (16.1 E), south of 48.55 N

land.text: the Eastern March at first: 'between the river Enns and the Vienna Woods (Wienerwald)', at first coinciding with the Wachau (Mostviertel and the Danube valley)

predecessors.note: The Danube lands below the Enns were lost to the Magyars in 907 ('all East Frankish lands beyond the Enns river were lost') and reorganised after the Lechfeld of 955; Cliopatria's Principality of Hungary row runs 900-999. Repair of 2026-10-25: the land is now the Enns-Wienerwald strip only; the Vienna basin and the rest of Lower Austria come with the gains of 1043 and 1055 (ledger).

land.text: the Eastern March at first: 'between the river Enns and the Vienna Woods (Wienerwald)', at first coinciding with the Wachau (Mostviertel and the Danube valley)

predecessors.note: The march was a Bavarian frontier march until the Privilegium Minus of 1156.

land.text: Cliopatria's Habsburg shape from 1279 (79,610 km2) covers Austria and Styria; the 1260-1278 Habsburg shapes are Swiss

successors.note: At the Diet of Augsburg in 1282 Rudolf I granted the Austrian domains to his sons Albert and Rudolf II. Cliopatria draws the Habsburg Austria from 1279, three years before this dossier's end.

capitals.name: Melk
capitals.note: Infobox capital Melk; the text says the initial residence was probably Pöchlarn, though Melk may have been used earlier. Repair of 2026-10-25: the span now ends in 1107 because the residence moved to Klosterneuburg (next entry).

capitals.name: Klosterneuburg
capitals.note: 'The margraves' residence was moved down the Danube to Klosterneuburg until 1145' (Margraviate of Austria page); neither that page nor the Leopold III page dates the move. 1108 is the earliest dated trace: Leopold III founded Klosterneuburg Monastery then ('His most important foundation is Klosterneuburg (1108)') and 'expanded the settlement to become his residence'. Confidence 1 for the start year. Added in the repair of 2026-10-25 (review finding).

capitals.name: Vienna
capitals.note: 'until 1145, when Vienna became the official capital'; the duke 'took his residence at Vienna at the site of the later Hofburg Palace' (Duchy of Austria page).

rulers.name: Burchard
rulers.title: margrave
rulers.note: 'by about 960, he appointed Burchard as margrave'; first mentioned in sources 970; deposed by Otto II in 976.

rulers.name: Leopold VI
rulers.title: duke
rulers.note: Sole ruler of the Austrian and Styrian lands from 1198.

rulers.name: Frederick II the Warlike
rulers.title: duke
rulers.note: Killed at the Battle of the Leitha River in 1246; the Babenberg line became extinct in the male line.

rulers.name: Ottokar II of Bohemia
rulers.title: duke
rulers.note: Infobox 1251; invaded in 1250; king of Bohemia from 1253.

rulers.name: Rudolf I of Habsburg
rulers.title: king and duke
rulers.note: Granted the domains to his sons Albert and Rudolf II at Augsburg in 1282.

intersect.text: from the Enns (14.4 E) to the eastern edge of the Wienerwald (16.1 E), south of 48.55 N

correction.text: the Eastern March at first: 'between the river Enns and the Vienna Woods (Wienerwald)', at first coinciding with the Wachau (Mostviertel and the Danube valley)

keyframe_review.note: Repair of 2026-10-25 (review, blocking): the first shape is the Enns-Wienerwald strip, not all of Lower Austria. The Margraviate of Austria page: the march lay 'between the river Enns and the Vienna Woods (Wienerwald)' and 'at first coincided with the Wachau', 'shortly enlarged eastwards at least as far as the Wienerwald' (no date or ruler); the strip is the gazetteer's Niederösterreich cut by a polygon (14.4-16.12 E, 47.75-48.55 N), roughly the Mostviertel and the Wachau. The Vienna basin is on the page only as part of the earlier Pannonian march, and the Leitha and March frontier is undated. Original note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Austria row before the Habsburg shape of 1279; its Holy Roman Empire shape draws the Danube lands as imperial). The Duchy of Austria page: 'Initially small, the duchy roughly covered what is now Lower Austria'; the Margraviate page gives no area. Gazetteer Niederösterreich plus Wien is about 20,000 km2. The duchy 'expanded their territory into the old Bavarian lands west of the Enns River', reaching Linz, and in 1192 acquired Styria (personal union, ledger vassal tint); neither is dated on the pages, so Upper Austria is not drawn. Colonisation reached the Thaya under Ernest the Brave (1055-1075) and the Hungarian March was merged into Austria (undated border; already inside the Lower Austria region).

correction.text: the march from the Enns to the March (Morava) and the Leitha, without the northern Waldviertel and Weinviertel

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (review repair of 2026-10-25). The Adalbert page: Margrave Adalbert (1018-1055) 'extended the border as far as the rivers Morava/March and Leitha', without a date; he took part in the German-Hungarian War of summer 1030; neither the Adalbert nor the Margraviate page dates the step or the Vienna basin. 1043 is a bridge at confidence 1: the March of Styria page dates Henry III's conquest of land 'up to Pitten and the Leitha' to 1042/43. The shape is Lower Austria and Vienna south of 48.55 N; the northern Waldviertel and the northern Weinviertel follow in 1055. The land south of Wiener Neustadt is also drawn by march-of-styria's 1042 circle (about 15 of the 78 cells of Lower Austria overlap); that overlap is not resolved.

correction.text: Lower Austria and Vienna: the margraviate's extent by the 1055-1075 Thaya colonisation

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (review repair of 2026-10-25): all of Lower Austria and Vienna from 1055. The Margraviate page: 'Under Margrave Ernest the Brave (1055-1075), the colonisation of the northern Waldviertel up to the Thaya river' began, and the Hungarian March 'was merged into Austria' under him (no border or year). The Duchy of Austria page: the duchy 'roughly covered what is now Lower Austria' (1156). The 'expanded their territory into the old Bavarian lands west of the Enns River', reaching Linz, and the acquisition of Styria in 1192 (ledger vassal tint) are undated, so Upper Austria is not drawn. The gazetteer's Niederösterreich plus Wien is about 20,000 km2; neither page gives an area.

intersect.text: from the Enns (14.4 E) to the eastern edge of the Wienerwald (16.1 E), south of 48.55 N

region.text: the Eastern March at first: 'between the river Enns and the Vienna Woods (Wienerwald)', at first coinciding with the Wachau (Mostviertel and the Danube valley)

ledger.note: c. 960: Otto I sets up the Eastern March below the Enns. 'by about 960, he appointed Burchard as margrave' of a new Eastern March, after the Lechfeld (955); some sources give 970 and the infobox dates the margraviate from c. 970. The Danube lands had been lost beyond the Enns in 907. Repair of 2026-10-25: the founding shape is the Enns-Wienerwald strip.

intersect.text: from the Enns (14.4 E) to the eastern edge of the Wienerwald (16.1 E), south of 48.55 N

region.text: the Eastern March at first: 'between the river Enns and the Vienna Woods (Wienerwald)', at first coinciding with the Wachau (Mostviertel and the Danube valley)

ledger.note: c. 960: the Eastern March is a Bavarian march. 'by about 960, he appointed Burchard as margrave'; the page calls it the Bavarian Eastern March and has it 'elevated to a duchy independent from Bavaria by the Privilegium Minus' in 1156. Recorded from the vassal's side: the counterpart is the overlord, the mirror of stem-duchy-of-bavaria's vassal_start (counterpart margraviate-of-austria). Repair of 2026-10-25 (review, blocking).
976: Otto II deposes Burchard and appoints Leopold the Illustrious of the Babenberg house as margrave; the Babenbergs rule Austria until 1246.
996: the name Ostarrîchi first appears. It 'first appeared on a famous deed of donation issued by Emperor Otto III at Bruchsal in November 996'.

intersect.text: east of the Wienerwald to the Leitha and the March (Morava), south of 48.55 N

region.text: the Vienna basin, the Marchfeld and the southern Weinviertel east of the Wienerwald up to the rivers March (Morava) and Leitha

ledger.note: Between 1018 and 1055 (bridged at 1043): the march reaches the March (Morava) and the Leitha. The Adalbert page: he 'extended the border as far as the rivers Morava/March and Leitha' (no date; margrave 1018-1055); the Margraviate page gives the Vienna basin only as part of the earlier Pannonian march and the Hungarian frontier 'along the Morava (March) and Leitha rivers' without a date. The year 1043 is the March of Styria page's date for Henry III's conquest up to the Leitha (1042/43); this event rests on a silence and is a gap, not a fault (confidence 1). The land is the Vienna basin, the Marchfeld and the southern Weinviertel; the counterpart is kingdom-of-hungary (Cliopatria 1000-1546), which draws none of it. Repair of 2026-10-25 (review, blocking).

intersect.text: north of 48.55 N up to the Thaya

region.text: the northern Waldviertel up to the Thaya river (colonised 1055-1075) and the northern Weinviertel

ledger.note: 1055: the northern Waldviertel and the northern Weinviertel come into the march. 'Under Margrave Ernest the Brave (1055-1075), the colonisation of the northern Waldviertel up to the Thaya river' (Margraviate of Austria page; a footnote adds that Austria did not colonise Moravia in the 11th century); the same page says the Hungarian March 'was merged into Austria' under him, with no border. The year is the start of Ernest's reign and of the colonisation, which ran to 1075; the northern Weinviertel is the researcher's reading. Repair of 2026-10-25 (review, blocking).

1108 (bridged): the residence moves from Melk to Klosterneuburg. 'The margraves' residence later was moved down the Danube to Klosterneuburg until 1145' (Margraviate page, undated); the Leopold III page dates only the foundation of Klosterneuburg Monastery to 1108 and says he made the settlement his residence. Confidence 1. Repair of 2026-10-25 (review).
1145: Vienna becomes the capital; the residence had stayed at Klosterneuburg 'until 1145, when Vienna became the official capital'.

1156: Austria becomes a duchy. The Babenberg margraviate was elevated by the Privilegium Minus on 17 September 1156, 'independent from Bavaria', as an inheritable fief with Henry Jasomirgott its first duke.

region.text: Lower Austria and Vienna: the margraviate's extent by the 1055-1075 Thaya colonisation

ledger.note: 17 September 1156: 'Austria was elevated to a duchy independent from Bavaria by the Privilegium Minus' (Margraviate of Austria page); the mirror of stem-duchy-of-bavaria's vassal_end. Repair of 2026-10-25 (review, blocking).

region.text: the Styrian lands in the south, ruled in personal union with Austria

ledger.note: 1192: the Babenbergs acquire Styria. After the death of Ottokar IV, whom they had signed the Georgenberg Pact with in 1186, they 'acquired the adjacent Styrian lands in the south'; the lands were ruled in personal union with Austria until 1918. Drawn as the lighter tint because Styria stays a separate duchy (see duchy-of-styria).

region.text: the Styrian lands in the south, ruled in personal union with Austria

ledger.note: 1246: the personal union with Styria ends with the Babenbergs. 'The Austrian Babenbergs became extinct in 1246' and Styria became a disputed vacant imperial fief; in 1254 it 'passed quickly through the hands of Hungarian kings' (Duchy of Styria page), then to Bohemia in 1260. Ottokar II held both lands from the early 1250s, but the personal union of 1192 is the Babenbergs' (Georgenberg Pact). duchy-of-styria (eu-09) records 1192 as a rename and carries no matching relation. Repair of 2026-10-25 (review).

1251: Ottokar II of Bohemia takes Austria. The Babenberg line ended with Frederick II's death at the Leitha in 1246; after Gertrude's second husband died, Ottokar II invaded in 1250 (infobox reign 1251) and became king of Bohemia in 1253, ruling the Bohemian, Moravian, Austrian and Styrian lands.
1276: Rudolf of Habsburg takes the dominion. 'took over the dominion as the first monarch of the Habsburg dynasty in 1276'; Ottokar was killed at the Marchfeld on 26 August 1278.

region.text: the Bavarian Eastern March below the Enns, 'roughly what is now Lower Austria'

ledger.note: 1282: Rudolf I grants the Austrian domains to his sons Albert and Rudolf II at the Diet of Augsburg; Albert I's reign is listed as 1282-1291. The Habsburg duchy of Austria continues under the House of Habsburg.

wars.name: Battle of the Leitha River
belligerents: opponent not named on the page
wars.outcome: Duke Frederick II was killed in 1246 and the Babenberg line became extinct in the male line; the succession was fought over until Ottokar II of Bohemia took the duchy in 1250-1251.
wars.note: The page gives no month or day and does not name the opponent.

wars.name: Battle on the Marchfeld

zones.text: the Bavarian Eastern March below the Enns, 'roughly what is now Lower Austria'

wars.outcome: Rudolf I took over the dominion in 1276; Ottokar II was killed by the united Austrian and Hungarian forces at the Marchfeld on 26 August 1278.

certainty.note: No treaty draws the march's frontiers on the pages opened; the Privilegium Minus names no counties and the page gives no borders for Austria.

sources.title: Privilegium Minus
sources.note: 8 and 17 September 1156; Austria 'a Bavarian frontier march'.

sources.title: Duchy of Austria
sources.note: 1156 duchy, area, Vienna, dukes, 1186 and 1192 Styria, 1250-1251 Ottokar, 1276, 1278, 1282.

sources.note: Reign 1018-1055; extended the border to the March (Morava) and Leitha, undated; 1030 war; read for the thin finding.

sources.note: 1180 duchy, 1186 Georgenberg Pact, 1192 union with Austria, Babenberg extinction 1246, Hungary 1254; silent on Traungau and Pitten; read for the 1246 end of the union.

sources.title: Leopold III, Margrave of Austria
sources.note: Klosterneuburg Monastery founded 1108; residence expanded; silent on the move and on Melk; read for the capitals finding.

notes:
Three pages opened (budget 2-5). The dossier runs from the Eastern March (c. 960) to the Habsburg grant of 1282 so that it covers the years 1251-1282 that Cliopatria draws only from 1279; eu-09 (Habsburg Austria) can chain from its end. Not settled: the start (960 by 'about 960', c. 970 by the infobox, first margrave 970 by the sources) and the earliest border; the Hungarian March and Thaya colonisation (1055-1075, no border given); the date of the growth west of the Enns to Linz (page undated, so Upper Austria is not drawn; Bavaria's keyframe keeps Oberösterreich until 1255); the 1246-1251 interregnum and its claimants; the margraves 976-1141 (the pages give no list, so the ruler strip is partial). The Margraviate is a Bavarian dependency to 1156: the Bavaria dossier draws it as a vassal tint. The Third Crusade, Wiener Neustadt and the Georgenberg Pact (1186) are on the Duchy page without territorial effect.

Repair of 2026-10-25 (review findings): (1) vassal_start 960 and vassal_end 1156 (month 9) with stem-duchy-of-bavaria are added, recorded from the vassal's side (counterpart = the overlord), mirroring Bavaria's. (2) The first shape is the Enns-Wienerwald strip (Margraviate page: 'between the river Enns and the Vienna Woods', at first the Wachau); the Vienna basin, Marchfeld and southern Weinviertel are a 1043 gain at confidence 1 (the Adalbert page gives the March/Morava and Leitha extension within his reign 1018-1055 without a year; 1043 is the March of Styria page's date of Henry III's conquest to the Leitha); the northern Waldviertel and Weinviertel are the 1055 gain (Ernest the Brave's colonisation to the Thaya, 1055-1075). The Hungarian March merger under Ernest is undated and has no border. (3) The 1192 Styria tint ends in 1246 (Babenberg extinction; Duchy of Styria page), not at Hungary's 1254 or Bohemia's 1260; the Duchy of Styria page is silent on the Traungau and Pitten. (4) Capitals: Klosterneuburg is added between Melk and Vienna, with an undated move bridged at 1108 (the Leopold III page dates only the monastery's foundation); the Melk span ends 1107. (5) Page budget: this repair opened three more pages (Adalbert, Duchy of Styria, Leopold III) beyond the original three because the review asked for them. (6) Open: march-of-styria's 1042 circle (16.0 E 47.7 N, 45 km) covers about 15 of the 78 cells of Lower Austria (Pitten, Wiener Neustadt and the southern Vienna basin) that this dossier also draws; the March of Styria page says the conquered land lay 'up to Pitten and the Leitha', so the south of Lower Austria was probably Styrian from 1042 to 1192, but the circle is coarse and neither dossier was changed for it.
